key_insight: A morphogenetic graph-growth rule, inspired by biological development, can generate mechanical lattices and enable inverse design through a GCNN surrogate.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to expand mechanical metamaterial databases and rapidly target stiffness or deformation performance without exhaustive finite-element search.
method: Start from a 3×3×3 dot-matrix of 27 candidate nodes and grow the lattice sequentially via cross-layer and intra-layer connections.
Represent each lattice as a graph and train a 3-layer GCNN with dual global pooling to learn topology-to-stiffness mapping.
Use the GCNN as a fast surrogate for sampling and inverse design; extend the idea to curved horseshoe-shaped beams for shape programming.
evidence_signal: The inverse-design example targeted 1000 MPa and produced a design predicted at 1042.43 MPa, which finite-element analysis validated at 1027.49 MPa.
watch_item: Performance depends on the diversity and coverage of the generated lattice database, so extrapolation to unseen topologies or material behaviors may be limited.
paper_title: Growth-Inspired Graph Generation and Inverse Design of Mechanical Lattices via Dot Matrices Database Augmentation and GCNN
